title: HELIX Govern: Data Governance Maturity Model
description: A self-assessment framework for higher education institutions to evaluate their data governance maturity across five dimensions. Aligned with HELIX conformance levels.

dimensions.description: How well the institution has adopted shared data definitions and standards.

levels.1_initial: No shared data model. Each system and department defines data independently. Terminology varies across reports.
levels.2_developing: Awareness of HELIX Core exists. Some teams reference HELIX resources as a conceptual model but data lake does not conform.
levels.3_defined: Data lake silver layer maps to HELIX Core schemas for at least 3 core domains. HELIX terminology code sets are used for key attributes. Validation passes for core resources.
levels.4_managed: All core domains map to HELIX Core. Schema evolution process is in place. New resources are contributed back to the community. Extension points are used for institution-specific attributes.
levels.5_optimizing: Full HELIX Core conformance. Institution serves as a reference implementation. Cross-institutional data sharing is possible with minimal additional mapping.

dimensions.description: The presence and effectiveness of governance roles, councils, and decision-making processes.

levels.1_initial: No formal governance roles. Data decisions are ad hoc, made by whoever is closest to the system.
levels.2_developing: Some governance roles exist informally. A data governance council may have been proposed but does not meet regularly.
levels.3_defined: HELIX Govern roles are mapped to institutional positions. A data governance council meets regularly. Domain stewards are identified for core domains.
levels.4_managed: Governance roles have clear authority and accountability. Escalation paths are documented. Stewards actively maintain HELIX resource definitions and quality rules. CDO reports governance health metrics.
levels.5_optimizing: Governance is embedded in institutional culture. Data literacy programs are widespread. Governance decisions are informed by metrics and continuous improvement.

dimensions.description: The systematic measurement and improvement of data quality.

levels.1_initial: Data quality is unknown or anecdotal. Issues are discovered reactively when reports look wrong.
levels.2_developing: Some data quality checks exist in ETL pipelines but are not systematic. No quality dashboards or SLAs.
levels.3_defined: HELIX quality rules are implemented for core domains. Quality metrics are measured and visible. Critical rule failures block downstream processing.
levels.4_managed: Quality SLAs are established per domain. Root cause analysis is performed for quality failures. Quality trends are tracked over time. Stewards review quality dashboards monthly.
levels.5_optimizing: Predictive quality monitoring. Automated remediation for common issues. Quality is measured at the source (ERP) and at each transformation layer. Institution contributes quality patterns back to HELIX community.

dimensions.description: How data is classified, access is controlled, and compliance obligations are met.

levels.1_initial: No formal classification. Access is based on system permissions inherited from ERP. FERPA compliance is handled ad hoc.
levels.2_developing: Awareness of classification tiers exists. Some sensitive data is tagged but classification is inconsistent across systems.
levels.3_defined: HELIX data classification tiers (public, internal, confidential, restricted) are applied to all resources via the meta block. Access policies are documented per classification level.
levels.4_managed: Classification is enforced automatically in the data lake (e.g., column-level access controls based on meta.classification). Access auditing is in place. FERPA/GDPR compliance is demonstrable.
levels.5_optimizing: Dynamic classification that adjusts based on context (e.g., aggregated data may be lower classification than individual records). Privacy-preserving analytics (differential privacy, synthetic data) are available.

dimensions.description: The institution's investment in data skills, data-informed decision-making, and governance culture.

levels.1_initial: Data use is limited to a few technical staff. Most decisions are based on intuition or anecdote.
levels.2_developing: Interest in data-informed decision-making exists at the leadership level. Some training programs are available.
levels.3_defined: Data literacy training is available and encouraged. Key stakeholders understand HELIX resource definitions and can interpret quality metrics. Self-service analytics tools are deployed.
levels.4_managed: Data literacy is expected as a competency for leadership roles. Faculty and staff regularly use governed data for decisions. Governance participation is recognized in performance evaluations.
levels.5_optimizing: Data is a strategic asset recognized at the board level. The institution publishes open data sets. Research and teaching incorporate institutional data. Data literacy is part of student learning outcomes.

assessment_guidance.how_to_use: For each dimension, select the level that best describes the institution's CURRENT state. Be honest — this is a diagnostic tool, not a scorecard. Most institutions beginning their HELIX journey will be at levels 1-2 across most dimensions.
assessment_guidance.scoring: There is no single score. The value is in identifying which dimensions need the most attention and creating a roadmap for improvement.
assessment_guidance.frequency: Assess annually, or when a major data initiative (ERP migration, lake implementation, governance program launch) begins or completes.

helix_conformance_alignment.Aligned (Level 2): Level 3 in Data Model & Standards; levels 2-3 elsewhere
helix_conformance_alignment.Contributor (Level 4): Level 4+ in Data Model & Standards; level 3+ elsewhere
